title: On the Positivity of the Products of Positive Primitive Forms
summary: Let $(V_i,ω_i)$ be real symplectic vector spaces and let $Ω_i\in\mathcal U^+(V_i)$ in the sense of Haiden. We prove that $p_1^*Ω_1\wedge p_2^*Ω_2$ belongs to $\mathcal U^+(V_1\oplus V_2)$ whenever one factor has real dimension at most six. There are forms $Ω\in\mathcal{U}^+(\mathbb{R}^6)\setminus\mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{ag}}(\mathbb{R}^6)$ for which $p_1^*Ω\wedge\cdots\wedge p_k^*Ω$ belongs to $\mathcal{U}^+$ for every $k\geq 1$; hence a conjecture of Kontsevich does not hold in complex dimension three.
